analysis.title: Central bank preview: A global pause rather than an end to tightening
key_insights: Markets expect the Fed, ECB and BoJ to hold at their October meetings, but pricing still points to further tightening, so the holds are read as pauses and not the start of easing.
Pictet's global composite central bank indicator rose to 35% at end-September, as the cumulative balance of hikes relative to cuts keeps rising across the central banks covered.

Fed funds futures imply about an 87% probability of no change on 28 October. By December 2026 futures price roughly one 25 bp hike from the current 3.75%-4.00% range to 4.00%-4.25%, then two more in 2027.
The Atlanta Fed GDP nowcast was 3.5% on 27 October, down from about 5% in late September, while the core PCE nowcast rose to 3.15% from 3.0%. Softer growth is not weak enough to justify a cut.

US September headline CPI rose to 3.74% from 3.40% in August, with energy contributing 1.31 percentage points. Core CPI edged up to 2.56% from 2.45%, with core services the largest underlying contributor at 1.91 percentage points.

September payrolls rose 29,000 versus 162,000 in August, and unemployment edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%. August JOLTS openings fell to 7.08 million from 7.34 million. Pictet reads this as slowing hiring, not a sharp deterioration.
University of Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1 in September from 51.7 in August, while five-year inflation expectations edged up to 3.4% from 3.3%.

The US 10-year yield is testing support at 4.93%-5.09%, including the rising 50-day SMA. A hold keeps the breakout intact with 5.37% as the next upside reference. A break below 4.93% brings 4.81% into view, then the 200-day SMA near 4.53%.
EUR/USD keeps a downside bias below former support at 1.1325 within a descending channel, helped by firmer US rate expectations relative to the euro area.
OIS implies about a 95% probability the ECB holds on 29 October, with about one 25 bp hike priced by December 2026 and close to three by September 2027. The deposit rate is 2.50%.
Euro-area inflation rose to 3.8% in September from 3.2% in August, while consumer confidence fell to -16.8 from -15.5. Inflation persistence is weighed against weak demand.

France's spread is 158.5 bp, wider than Italy at 116.8 bp, Greece at 99.2 bp, Spain at 66.1 bp and Portugal at 52.9 bp. Pictet attributes this to fiscal, political and debt-trajectory concerns, and notes Lagarde signalled no current intention to use the Transmission Protection Instrument for France.
The France-Germany 10-year spread reached the extended wave 3 target at 1.54. Support is 1.13-1.29, and while it holds the chart points to a possible wave 5 target at 2.00.

BoJ is expected to hold on 30 October with about 0.78 of a 25 bp hike priced by December. Cumulative pricing is 1.65 hikes by March 2027, 2.23 by June and 2.92 by September. The meeting includes an updated Outlook Report.

The Citi Economic Surprise Index for Japan fell from 21.9 at end-September to -8.5 on 23 October, its first negative reading since March, after September exports rose 16.7% y/y against a 20.1% consensus.
USD/JPY is capped by resistance at 157.75-158.55. A break above 158.55 targets 159.75 then 161.35-161.95. A move below 155.97 shifts focus to 152.56.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 3.40% in August and 3.36% in July, mostly from energy, which broke the summer disinflation trend.
Up from 2.45% in August. Core services contributed 1.91 percentage points, so the rise is not only energy.
Down from +162,000 in August. Pictet sees slowing hiring, not yet a sharp deterioration.
Down from 7.34 million in July, pointing to softer labour demand.
Down from 51.7 in August, widening the gap between resilient activity and household views.
Up from 3.3% in August, below May's 3.9%.
Down from about 5% in late September, still resilient.
Up from 3.0%, pointing to sticky underlying inflation. Official September PCE is due 29 October.
Futures price a hold on 28 October and about one 25 bp hike by December.
Up from 3.2% in August and 2.9% in July, complicating a weak growth backdrop.
Down from -15.5 in August, pointing to soft demand.
OIS prices a hold on 29 October and about one 25 bp hike by December.
Missed the 20.1% consensus, and the trade deficit was wider than expected.
First negative reading since March, less supportive of near-term BoJ tightening.

risk_factors: Energy-driven inflation spreading into core services keeps central banks restrictive.
A weak September payrolls print may be the start of a sustained cooling trend. September JOLTS is due 3 November and the October jobs report on 6 November.
Weak consumer sentiment alongside elevated inflation expectations leaves the Fed with a less reassuring backdrop.
Euro-area inflation persistence set against weak confidence complicates further ECB tightening.
French sovereign risk premium widening, with no ECB backstop signalled.
Japanese data no longer beating expectations may reduce support for BoJ tightening.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient activity, with the Atlanta Fed nowcast at 3.5% and core PCE nowcast at 3.15%, plus sticky core services inflation, supports further tightening, which futures price at one hike by December.
tension_points.bear_case: Payrolls slowed to 29,000, unemployment rose to 4.2%, job openings fell and consumer sentiment dropped to 48.1, which could limit how much restraint the economy absorbs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below 4.93% in the US 10-year yield would weaken the hawkish breakout setup. September JOLTS on 3 November and the October jobs report on 6 November will show whether the payroll slowdown is sustained.

tension_points.bull_case: Euro-area inflation at 3.8% supports keeping policy restrictive, with about one hike priced by December.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumer confidence at -16.8 points to soft demand, complicating further tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further data showing whether inflation pressures are broadening or remain largely energy-led.

tension_points.bull_case: A still-cautious BoJ and hawkish Fed favour dollar-yen strength, and markets price about 0.78 of a hike by December.
tension_points.bear_case: Japan's economic surprise index turned negative at -8.5 and exports missed consensus, which is less supportive of near-term tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break above 158.55 in USD/JPY would strengthen upside momentum, while a move below 155.97 would point to renewed weakness.
